title: Is the theory's own gravity of strength one in lattice units (a/l_P = 1)?
plain: The theory declares its lattice spacing to be the Planck length, as a choice of ruler. What nobody has shown is that the theory's own gravity, measured in that ruler, has strength one. The one route that said yes needs a premise the four axioms do not contain, and a June probe found that premise to be the ruler choice in disguise.

title: From the cutoff scale to the observed scales: Lambda_QCD << 1/a and the coupling transport
plain: Put a strongly coupled force theory on a Planck-size lattice and all its own scales sit near the Planck scale. The strong-force scale we observe is about 6 x 10^18 times lower. The repo bridges the gap by declaring the lattice coupling to be the coupling at 246 GeV, and by a formula for the weak scale with open pieces. Ordinary running from the lattice value blows up far above 246 GeV. No note derives the bridge.

title: g_bare = 1 (beta = 6): convention or input, and the two identifications behind it
plain: Every coupling in the chain starts from "the bare gauge coupling is 1", meaning the lattice gauge action has strength beta = 6. The repo calls this a harmless convention in one place and an open gate in another. The algebra shows only that g and beta are two names for one number. Fixing the number needs two undemonstrated identifications. It is not harmless: the weak-scale formula goes as its 32nd power.

title: The plaquette value and the vertex power, the declared inputs of the alpha_s chain
plain: Even granting g = 1, turning it into the strong coupling needs two more things the repo lists as declared, not derived. One is the average plaquette of the SU(3) lattice at beta = 6, known only from Monte Carlo (0.5934), with no analytic route ready. The other is which power of that number to use. The other choice changes the weak-scale formula by a factor of eight.

title: Weak and hypercharge couplings, the mixing angle and the fine-structure constant
plain: The weak and hypercharge couplings at the lattice scale (1/4 and 1/5), and so the mixing angle (4/9 at the lattice), are recorded as formal hypotheses, not derivations. Carrying SU(2) to the weak scale meets an infinite-coupling barrier. The low-energy fine-structure constant needs extra running with thresholds, and the size of atoms needs the electron mass, which is a separate free input. No electromagnetic number is derived.

title: Scale dynamics cannot produce dimensionless ratios: mass moduli stay free inputs
plain: A tempting way to get mass ratios is to let couplings "run" from a high-scale value. The lane tested this in a toy: running only moves the free number to the starting value, so you still put in one number per sector. The lepton mass scale is likewise one free real number, and the Higgs boundary condition is admitted. No mass ratio is fixed by scale dynamics, and the flavour lanes have not fixed them by structure either.

title: The record-dynamics lane keeps adding free dimensionless constants
plain: The axioms give no numbers for how strongly neighbouring records affect one another. The September work on moving records keeps finding one more free number: an overall binding scale, the gravity-like stiffness, the ratio that sets how fast field waves travel, a formation rate. The owner calls the binding scale "a primitive like planck". A proposal to fix it by a no-privilege argument exists but is not adopted, and the proof of long-range order does not reach that value.

title: Order-one lattice-scale numbers against a tiny observed vacuum: the tuning demands
plain: With a Planck-size lattice and order-one numbers, the vacuum carries order-one lattice-scale energy and shape stiffness. The gravity probe found that a field laid over the grid gets mass-like terms of Planck size unless at least two more numbers are tuned, on top of the cosmological constant. That is fitting under another name.
